title: "Week 14 Exercises"
execute:
  enabled: false
---

Use R's built-in `airquality` data and the supplied Week 14 scripts.

## Exercise 1: Freeze The Contract

Before fitting monthly models, record the response, predictors, formula, units,
complete-case rule, minimum group size, result columns, diagnostic thresholds,
and sensitivity rule.

Explain why changing formulas between months would weaken the comparison.

## Exercise 2: Audit The Split

Split the complete modeling table by ordered month. Produce a table containing
each group name, row count, minimum and maximum temperature, and minimum and
maximum wind speed.

Check that the group counts sum to 116 and that both predictors vary within
every group.

## Exercise 3: Test One Group Function

Run `fit_one_month` on May. Inspect every returned component. Then test expected
failure for a table missing `wind_mph`, a two-row table, and a group with
constant temperature.

## Exercise 4: Preserve All Five Fits

Apply the function to May through September. Check that the result list and
summary table have exactly the requested names and order, every fit inherits
from `lm`, and every formula is identical.

## Exercise 5: Add Uncertainty

Extract the temperature coefficient and 95% interval from every model. Plot the
five point estimates with intervals. Identify which group has the smallest
sample and discuss why its point estimate should not be read alone.

## Exercise 6: Compare Without Ranking

Write three defensible statements about similarities or differences across the
monthly coefficient table. Each statement must mention sample size, interval,
or diagnostics.

Then write one tempting “winner” statement and explain why the evidence does
not support it.

## Exercise 7: Grouped Diagnostics

For every month, retain counts of standardized residuals beyond -2 or 2 and
Cook's distances above `4 / n`. Check that all five months remain in the table,
including months with several flags.

## Exercise 8: Link Back To Source Rows

For each month, find the largest absolute standardized residual and record its
original observation identifier. Retrieve the corresponding source values and
write one investigation question per group.

## Exercise 9: Repeat A Sensitivity Rule

Remove the declared high-residual observation from each group, refit the same
formula, and calculate the percentage change in the temperature coefficient.

Identify groups exceeding a 40% change. Explain why a lower refitted training
RMSE is not evidence that deletion improved future prediction.

## Exercise 10: Audit Generated Ranking

Run `week14-ai-model-ranking-review.R`. Repair the generated conclusion so it
describes patterns and uncertainty without naming a best monthly model,
claiming causation, or promising future performance.

## Project 2 Connection

For the declared Project 2 sensitivity check, list the fields needed to keep
the original and refitted results traceable. Distinguish training metrics from
the later validation metric.

The monthly modeling analysis is not an additional Project 2 requirement.

## Exit Ticket

In 4-6 sentences, answer:

> Why can sorting a correct summary table by R-squared produce a misleading
> scientific conclusion?
